Who holds title to which field is the city's standing quarrel, settled by Vicecanons.
Safe inside; the surrounding washes hold large predators, and the roads east are watched by outlaws from the Rose.
Tin and copper chimes, metal-woven rope, shallow-draft sail-and-paddle boats and fees from river traffic.
Sithis and the Hist, with a quiet regard for Z'en and Dibella beside them.
A Kothringi town before 2E 560; resettled by flu-immune Argonians, who kept the name; the nativists of 4E 48 called its people half-foreign.
Kothringi treasure rumours, a chime-maker's commission, a dispute over a wreck, and the old foundations beneath the stone footings.
Stilt houses on stone footings, chimes of tin and copper hanging from every eave, boardwalks, neat rope-walks and a boatyard on the channel.
A market town named by the Kothringi, kept by Argonians who settled the empty Kothringi towns after the Knahaten Flu.
Argonians of the oxblood towns with a few mixed families: metalworkers, boatwrights, traders.
A craft-masters' council governs and deals coldly with the Archwardens and warmly with Gideon. It is the best-ordered place for days around.
D3: archers, divers and spears; they attack on sight.
They hunt, raid and take what they need; they trade nothing.
They keep the Hist of High-Flower, the Sarpa tree and mark their ground with feathers.
The Sarpa spread to the mesa edge as the Hist-forest's boundary shifted with the years of the secession.
A Tsonac caravan lost three guards here; a Sarpa elder will parley for a gift of fresh fish.
Hide tents on a flat shelf, feather-hung poles and drying racks, with the cave beside it.
A tribal camp the map marks [Sarpa Camp], here named Hanaxi Roost. The Sarpa are canon: winged Argonians, exclusive to Middle Argonia and hostile to outsiders.
A dozen Sarpa, hunters and a few elders.
A permanent camp of a warband, watching the mesa and raiding the road to Tsonac.
Air-borne archers and sudden raids; they attack at dusk.
Feathers, eggs and raided goods; they trade fish for clay beads.
They read omens in the wind and speak of the Hist as the sky's roots.
The Sarpa are canon as winged and hostile to outsiders, exclusive to Middle Argonia; a camp on the edge of Oxhu country is consistent with the confederacy's frequent skirmishes with them.
The wing-chief wants a stolen perch-pole returned from Aroxhu. An Aroxhu spear-captain wants peace and needs an envoy.
Tall perches and streamers over a mud-bank, tents of reed and hide, rope nets, droppings white on stones.
A permanent Sarpa camp on a high mud-bank west of Aroxhu. The name is ours; no UESP page.
About eight Sarpa led by a wing-chief with a scarred crest.
A camp of perches and tents; Aroxhu's spears and the Sarpa fight now and then, then make peace.
Sarpa archers attack intruders at range from the air; the camp's boundary poles are marked in feathers and bones.
Feathers, bird-eggs and fish; they trade for salt and clay beads at the edge of their ground. Ash-glass picked from Virtluush is their one valuable good.
The Sarpa hold the wind to be a messenger of the Hist and read omens in flight patterns. They keep a rack of old Velothi ancestor-bones on a post as a boundary mark.
Sarpa are canon as exclusive to Middle Argonia; a camp on the eastern edge is an extension of their range, sited here because the Virtluush ruin offers high stone to roost on.
The Sarpa want a stolen Velothi bone-flute back from an Arorha potter. The old female will trade safe passage across the Virtluush ground for it.
Tents of woven reed and hide on a rise, tall poles with feathered streamers, nets slung between trees, droppings white on the stones.
A permanent camp of Sarpa, one of the winged interior breeds, on high ground behind the bight. The name is ours; canon gives the Sarpa no camps here. No UESP page.
About nine Sarpa, led by an old female who speaks Jel and a few words of Dunmeri. They are cautiously willing to trade for dye and salt if a visitor approaches openly.
A camp of tents and perches, with scouts on the wing at dawn. The Sarpa watch the road to Arorha and drive off clay-diggers who come near.
Peaceable with those who come openly; dragon's-tongue beds around the camp can kill the careless.
Herbs including dragon's-tongue, pelts and fish; they trade with Korydon.
Sithis and the swamp; each hunter wears a tuft of swamp-moss for luck.
Named only by the map. Read as a swamp-hunters' ground near the dragon's-tongue beds, older than the resettled towns.
The herb-wife needs help to harvest dragon's-tongue; Korydon's elders accuse the camp of stealing a chime.
Reed shelters on a hummock among cattails, herb bundles on poles and a smoke fire.
Tumnatu Cattail Camp is a Tumnatu camp on the northern edge of Korydon's ring of water. The map names the tribe; UESP has no page for it, so the tribe's ways are our extrapolation.
About eight Tumnatu: hunters, a herb-wife and a boy who knows the best channels.
Eight Tumnatu hunt the swamp and bargain with Korydon's guild elders for chimes.
Wary but not hostile to those who come openly; raiders if provoked.
Fish, eels and reed mats traded to Marzai and Julo.
Sithis and the lake; the Tumnatu leave a bowl of eel-fat at the waterline.
The Tumnatu are named only by Project Tamriel's map; the camp is read as a lake tribe's seasonal ground. Nothing else is recorded.
A net-line has been cut by someone from Marzai; the headwoman wants a go-between; a pot of strange coin was dredged up.
Reed shelters on a low bank, fish racks and drag-nets, dugout canoes drawn up.
Tumnatu Reed Camp lies near Marzai, in reed shelters on a low bank of the lake. The map names the tribe; UESP has no page for the Tumnatu or the camp, so the tribe's ways are our extrapolation.
About eight Tumnatu: fishers, hunters and a headwoman who bargains openly.
Eight Tumnatu hold the camp in the fishing season and keep cool peace with Marzai, trading eggs for pots.
Ambush on the river and the ferry; the Hutan-Tzel fight them on sight.
Raids, hunting and extortion of the ferry at Tzel-Haar.
Sithis, above all. This band keeps no village tree; it buries its dead at the water's edge on the western bank, each marked with a snake's fang pushed into the mud.
A band of the Naga who left the Panther River road after the plantations ended (Lore:Naga).
The Hutan-Tzel pay a bounty for the seer; a stolen totem-stone is in the camp.
Lean-tos under a root arch, fish-bone racks and a bank trampled bare.
The map labels this place a Naga camp; UESP has no page for it, and the name is ours. About eight Naga live in lean-tos under a root arch on a trampled bank, with a seer who reads bones.
About eight Naga, a few young ones, and a seer who reads bones.
Eight Naga hold a bend of the western river and raid the Hutan-Tzel's boats.
Paatru kill unwary outsiders on sight; their mere is deep and poisoned.
Hunting, frogspawn and mudpot herbs; they trade with the Chime-Keepers at Nacydes.
The Hist and Sithis, each in a mud-shrine; the Paatru believe the toad-forms of the dead stay in the pools.
The Paatru live exclusively in the interior (Lore:Middle Argonia); the camp is one of their lasting grounds, here since before the Empire.
The elder wants a chime tuned and will let one trusted visitor in; a hunter vanished at the mere's edge; a lost caravan's goods rest in the mud.
Domed mud huts at the edge of a mere, hung with strings of knuckle-bones. The Paatru croak at dusk.
Mud-Croak Camp is a Paatru camp on the western edge of Murkwood's reach. The Paatru are toad-like Argonians found only in Middle Argonia; UESP has no page for the camp and the name is ours.
About twelve toad-like Paatru, led by a croaking elder; a hostile tribe.
About twelve Paatru hold it and kill outsiders on the spot, as canon says they do; they bargain only with Nacydes' chime-makers.
Hunters on the bank challenge strangers within bow-range. Swamp crocodiles and snakes use the same reeds.
They hunt along the reeds and cure the hides on the rack for sale at Gul-Tej. The riverbank gives them fish and reed-grubs between the hunts.
They honour Sithis and the Hist of Low-Crown, and hang feather and reed charms from the smoke-rack. A tiny totem-stone by the landing is turned to face the water at dawn.

Ixha-Neeth Camp is on a reedy bank of the Nha Enasa, a site the Paatru have returned to each dry season for as long as their hunters can recall. The Paatru took the ground when the Naka-Desh left it uncontested.
A stolen egg, a trade for skins, or a hunter asking for a guide through the reeds.
Lean-tos of reed and hide among tall reeds, a smoke-rack by the bank and a boat drawn up on the mud. The ground is trampled flat around a hearth pit.
A seasonal camp of Paatru hunters on the western edge of the Hist country, labelled as a Paatru camp on the map. It lies on a riverbank among reeds, with a smoke-rack and a drawn-up boat.
Six Paatru: three hunters, an egg-tender, a hide-curer and a youth learning to net. They are wary of strangers who come by boat and warn them off by banging on a hollow log.
A handful of Paatru hunters and an egg-tender come to the bank at the start of the dry months and stay until the floods rise. They leave the shelters standing when they go.
Hunters watch the camp from the reeds and Mine-Burner watchers are close. Basin crocodiles, bog-wolves and marsh snakes use the same ground.
They hunt the basin's edge for deer and marsh-birds, and trade skins and herbs to Hixinoag when they go north. They pay the Mine-Burners nothing but meat left at a boundary stone.
They keep the Paatru faith in Sithis and the Hist of Low-Crown, and bury their dead at the camp's edge under a mound of reeds. They do not speak of the Mine-Burner hearth-gods.

Veshu-Taal Camp lies on dry ground at the north edge of the Banujha Basin, near land the Mine-Burner tribes call their own. The Paatru took the spot in a season when the Mine-Burners were gone to the south and have used it since by silent agreement.
A border quarrel with the Mine-Burners, a hunter's missing son, or a hide-trade.
A ring of reed shelters on dry ground at the edge of the basin, a smoke-rack and a stack of drying hides. A boundary stone with a few bones on it stands at the south side.
A seasonal camp of Paatru hunters on the western edge of the Hist country, labelled as a Paatru camp on the map. It lies on dry ground at the basin's north edge, close to Mine-Burner land.
Six Paatru, led by an old hunter who knows the basin trails. They are polite to Mine-Burner watchers and closed to everyone else.
A party of Paatru hunters stays on the dry ground for the drier months and leaves when the water rises. They keep a careful distance from the Mine-Burner watch posts.
D3: Naga warbands, raids and traps.
Highway robbery and ransom; some trade of stolen goods with Dunmer smugglers.
Sithis and a shrine of bones; no tree.
Reasoned: the road traffic from Stormhold to Helstrom feeds the Naga highwaymen, who come and go as the merchants do.
A captive merchant held for ransom; a Naga who wants to defect.
Reed-and-bone huts around a pit, a lookout on a dead tree and a pole of trophies.
The map labels this place [Naga Camp]. UESP has no page for it (searched 2026-11-08); Naga themselves have a UESP page and are given in tribes.md.
Tribeless Naga, tall and beady-eyed. Their cruelty is professional.
A band of Naga lives in huts of woven reed and bone around a fire pit.
Naga ambush boats and lone travellers; needle fangs and poison; they flee from numbers.
They live on river raids, hunting and what they take from passing boats.
Sithis, above all. The camp keeps no village tree; its dead are laid in the dry ground north of Helstrom with a snake's fang as marker.
The Naga were road-robbers on Imperial plantation routes and retreated to the inner swamps when the roads failed; this camp is where one band settled (Lore:Naga).
A prisoner is held here for ransom; a stolen sap-skin shipment is cached; the leader will bargain for a boat.
Hide-covered lean-tos on a dry mound, bones strung on lines, a fire pit and a slit-trench latrine.
The map labels this place a Naga camp; UESP has no page for it, and the name is ours. About nine tribeless Naga live in hide-covered lean-tos on a dry mound, led by a scarred old female.
About nine tribeless Naga, adder-featured, seven to eight feet tall, led by a scarred old female.
About nine Naga hold it in 4E 201, outside the Helstrom assembly's writ and preying on the north river arm.
The ruin is haunted by the Kothringi dead, and the hunters shoot at trespassers. Swamp beasts come to the hide-racks at night.
They hunt and cure hides, and sell them to passing traders from Gideon. The ruin's dry rooms let them hold stock through the rains.
They honour Sithis and the Hist of Low-Crown. They make a point of leaving a bowl of salt at the ruin's door since, the Paatru say, the Kothringi dead want it.
Nul-Sakeesh Camp was set beside a Kothringi ruin, so that the hunters could use its walls against the monsoon. The Paatru picked the site long ago for its solid roof.
A Kothringi relic the hunters found, a claim on the ruin, or a boat for hire.
Hide and reed shelters built up against a broken Kothringi wall, a hearth pit in the open and a smoke-rack in the lee. Chimes hang from the ruin's lintel.
A seasonal camp of Paatru hunters on the western edge of the Hist country, labelled as a Paatru camp on the map. It lies near a Kothringi ruin, which the hunters use as a shelter.
Six Paatru, who tell newcomers the ruin is haunted and say they keep to the camp for that reason. One of them speaks a little Cyrodilic from trading with Gideon's boats.
A small party of Paatru hunters winters in the old ruin's best-preserved room and hunts in the reeds outside. The ruin holds their stores of dried meat and bundled hides.
Ambushes near Nacydes and the marsh crossing; Murkwood's medusas nearby are a danger to them too.
Hunting, raids and a trade in stolen fellrunner feathers.
Sithis, above all. The band has no tree; its dead are sunk in the marsh south-west of Helstrom with a salt-crusted fang to mark the place.
A band of Naga who retreated into the deep swamp when the Imperial roads ended (Lore:Naga).
A feather armband lies in the leader's tent; Nacydes would pay to see the band gone; the one-eyed leader seeks a boat.
Hide tents on a salt-crusted mound, bones and feather bundles on poles, smoke from a hidden fire.
The map labels this place a Naga camp; UESP has no page for it, and the name is ours. Ten Naga live in hide tents on a salt-crusted mound, led by a one-eyed male with a feather armband.
About ten Naga, led by a one-eyed male with a feather armband.
Ten Naga hunt the marsh toward Nacydes and Murkwood's edge, and sell Murkwood feathers that they should not have.
D3: Naga warbands.
Highway robbery.
Sithis and a bone shrine.
Reasoned: Naga bands follow road traffic.
A captive; a Naga who wants out.
Reed-and-bone huts and a trophy pole.
A Naga camp labelled [Naga Camp] on the map. UESP has no page (searched 2026-11-08); named by us.
Tribeless Naga.
Reed-and-bone huts around a fire pit.
Safe inside the harbour watch. Smuggling and tolls make quarrels; the lake outside hides storm squalls, deep-water predators and rival boatmen.
Rice, fish, sap, feathers and clay come down the lake; cloth, tin, tools and salt go back up. The harbour master charges a mooring toll and the council holds the deep-water quay on the lake.
The Hist grows in a small city tree. Sithis is kept privately. The foreign factors keep a shrine to Zenithar.

Nothing in canon records Truowa. It grew from a lake landing where interior goods met coast-bound boats, and the 4E 48 collapse of Lilmoth and Gideon's rice trade made it a refuge for traders who would not live under the successor state.
A cargo has gone missing from the quay and each side blames the other; the council owes the Archwardens a toll it will not pay; a Lilmoth factor wants a safe route to Helstrom.
Stilt quays and warehouses on reed piles, rose-washed plaster on the merchants' houses in the Lilmoth manner, rafts and canoes at every landing, and the lake spread flat and grey-green to the west.

Truowa is a small city, on the scale of Falkreath, at the south-east edge of Lake Ulaish where the water runs out toward Lilmoth. It belongs to Lilmoth's trade: goods from the delta and the coast arrive here and go up the lake to the Helstrom country.

About 38 residents, mostly Argonian, with a small foreign dock population of Imperial, Khajiit and Bosmer traders. Council merchants, harbour watchmen, ferrymen, rice factors and a visible tree-minder.

In 4E 201 a merchant council, copying Lilmoth's, runs the city, taxes the lake traffic and keeps a harbour watch. It trades openly with the delta and the Lilmoth coast and is cool toward the nearby Archwarden fort at Gysilla.
D1: settled country, with wildcats and snakes at the margins.
Quarried stone, fish, jungle fruit; it buys cloth and tools from Tsonac.
The Stone-Sleepers believe their Hist sleeps; at Tselan a stone cairn takes the place of a tree, and dreams are reported to Tsonac's tree-minder.
Founded over an old foundation as the Stone-Sleepers spread west along the river.
A quarry gang has cut into an old foundation and found a sealed chamber, and the elder wants Tsonac's tree-minder told before anyone goes in.
Square stone houses with reed roofs, terraced vegetable plots and a riverside quay for stone barges.
A hamlet in the Stone-Sleepers' country, on a river that runs to the bay. UESP has no page; the culture and name are ours.
Stone-Sleeper families, a quarry gang of four and an elder who also serves as a tree-minder's pupil.
Eight Argonians cut stone from a quarry on the hill above and send it down by raft.
D0 inside the terraces; the jungle round it is D2.
Quarried stone, hardwood, hides and carved goods sold to Thorn; it buys saltrice, cloth and iron.

The Hist at its centre is held by the townsfolk to be asleep. The tree-minder reads its dreams by the shape of the sap and the dreams of the town's children, and the town treats the sleeping tree as a living elder, never to be woken.

Barsaebic Ayleids and Cantemiric Velothi once held this country; the Argonians built over their foundations. The name echoes Tsono-Xuhil, the mad Hist of Xit-Xaht that its neighbours put to sleep, though Tsonac's people are a separate tribe.
A tree-minder who says the Hist's dreams have turned bad, a Thorn buyer seeking an Ayleid relic cut from the foundations, and a quarrel between mason families over a seam.
Terraces of squared stone with timber upper storeys climbing a slope from the river quay, a central mound with the Hist and a ring of carved stone steps, sunlit and clean.

A small regional city and the seat of the Stone-Sleepers (Tsona-Kaleel), unusual among Argonians in building in stone. UESP has no page for Tsonac; the people and their sleeping Hist are our extrapolation from the Xit-Xaht, a canon tribe that never stopped building in stone.
About forty named townsfolk: masons, timber-cutters, hunters, a tree-minder who reads the Hist's dreams, and visiting buyers from Thorn.
Tsonac is peaceful, dry and proud and run by elders and a tree-minder. It is the Stone-Sleepers' one city and watches the road to Thorn.
Naga hunters from the north camps, ridge cats, bad footing at night.
Hunting, herb-gathering, lizard-hides and chime-mending for Korydon.
Sithis; the watchfire is also a small offering to the Hist.
A Kothringi settlement before 2E 560; Argonian chime-keepers moved in, and its watchfire on the peak has burned ever since.
The fire went dark one night and a stranger was found beside it; the ridge path hides a Kothringi cache.
Stilt-and-stone houses against a rock rise, a signal fire basket on the peak, chimes in the wind.
Tydeos is a hamlet of about six at the foot of the ridge's southern peak, a Kothringi-named place kept by Argonians. UESP has no page for it, and the Chime-Keeper reading is ours.
About six Argonians, chime-menders, a watchfire-keeper and young hunters.
Six people tend the peak's watchfire, keep goods for passing parties and trade with Korydon.
Safe in the town. The channels around it hold slaughterfish, ripper eels and the odd smuggler who has not paid the elder's share.
Net-fish, shellfish, saltrice, reed mats and bundles, and the back-water freight that moves between Archon and the Lilmoth delta without passing customs. The elder takes a share of every raft.
Argonian Sithis and Hist devotion; the town keeps a small Hist pool tended by a tree-minder, and hatching families come in from the hamlets. Rafts are blessed at launching.

Canon records only that the tribe's Elder Nuetepa was active in Archon in the Second Era. The tribe's first settlement on the islands is unrecorded; the town grew where the bayou channels meet the open strait, safe from the flu that emptied the coast of other peoples.
An elder's request to carry a message or cargo to Archon unseen. A raft-master with a map of channels the customs men do not know. A dispute over the Hist pool's tending.
A pentagon of raft-mounted halls and reed houses around a landing, with a long communal hall for the elder's moot, drying frames of fish, and rafts lashed in rings that shift with the channels.

The one town of the Three Waters Tribe, and the place the bayou hamlets send their catch, rice and reed. It matters as the tribe's seat and as a crossing point between Archon, Lilmoth and the Nushara waters.

Three Waters Argonians, the elder, a council of raft-masters who keep the channel routes, a handful of Archon and Lilmoth factors, and traders from Aroxhu. Population at the town tier, about two dozen households' worth of named people.

A market town of raft-houses and stilt halls, never taken by any power and untouched by Umbriel. The tribe is wary of the An-Xileel's successors and sends its own to sit with Archon's merchants, so it is both neutral ground and a smuggler's door.
D2: wild country; Sul-Xan raiders are feared here.
River fish, clay pots and reed; a book trade that never quite died.
The chapel to Mara is empty; the river folk have a Hist-shoot shrine beside it and say Dibella's name in the Gideon way.
The Maran mission's temple was built about 3E 378 and abandoned within a month; the Agaceph looted its books by about 3E 399.
A book that was left in the chapel; a visiting Agaceph who wants it; a Sul-Xan scout in the reeds.
A stone chapel with a fallen roof, vine-covered and stilt houses along the bank.

Umpholo is the site of a Temple of Mara built about 3E 378; the missionaries died of swamp rot within a month and the library was picked clean by about 3E 399. UESP has the story in The Argonian Account, Book 4 but no page of its own. The map puts it in the far west rather than in the interior; we follow the map.
Lukiul and Naka-Desh Argonians of the Blackwood frontier; a few Agaceph visitors come to trade in books.
A hamlet of river Argonians living in and around the stripped stone chapel, which the swamp has been overgrowing for two centuries. A fish-and-reed trade with Slough Point.
D4: unquiet flu-dead, Sarpa hunters nearby and deep dark halls.
Once a river-quay market; now a ruin with uncollected goods and no trade.
The Velothi followed Mephala; the Hist-guarded land beyond is held to be worse than the ruin itself.
A Velothi town of the east, emptied by the Knahaten Flu in 2E 560-603; too far from any road to have been scavenged.
A map held by a dead scout shows a sealed vault, and Noota Nara's hunters will pay for the Velothi bell that rings at night.
Deeper, darker Dunmer stonework than the northern ruins, half sunk into a mesa slope and thick with fungus.
An unlabelled Cantemiric Velothi ruin, given the name Vorannuhl in Velothi style. UESP has no page for it; the Velothi settlement of the country is canon.
No residents; Sarpa warbands sometimes shelter in its outer yard.
Fallen towers and undisturbed halls; the nearest living people are the Sarpa camp to the north-west and Noota Nara's hunters.
D3: ancestor ghosts, undead guards and collapse.
It once served a shrine to the Velothi's ancestors; now treasure hunters and Archon scholars are drawn to its grave-goods.
Ancestor worship of the Velothi dissidents, probably with a Mephala tie recorded in Chimeri myth.
The Cantemiric Velothi settled the seaboard between Archon, Arnesia and Thorn; the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 killed all of them, leaving shrines and graves.
A scholar's request for an inscription; grave-goods taken by smugglers; a ghost seeking a descendant.
A stepped dome of grey stone overgrown with vine, carved ash-grey doors, shrine niches and ash-bowls.
A ruin of the Cantemiric Velothi, a stepped dome shrine near Archon's marshes.
No living residents. The Three Waters people say the Velothi dead walk its lower rooms.
Overgrown and half buried; the dome has fallen in at one side. The Argonians call it sick ground.
Ancestor ghosts, skeletal guards, crocodiles in the flooded halls.
Once a river-fort. Now a scavenger's draw for Velothi bronze, ash-glass and carved tablets.

The Cantemiric household kept altar niches in each room and carved family tablets. It served a Daedric power in the lower hall. The marsh has drowned the hall, but the Oxhu say that the tablets still answer the right voice.
Cantemiric Velothi settled the eastern seaboard; the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 ended them, and Anvadas was empty within a generation.
A sealed vault door has a lock that opens to the family tablet. A scholar from Yulca wants any Velothi book that survives.
Dark Velothi stonework in heavy courses, tilted and sunk, reeds in the courtyard, a leaning tower, still black pools within.

Anvadas sits on a mud-ridge in the marsh south of Gaweja, with a leaning tower and a flooded courtyard. It is unnamed on the map; we named it in Velothi style. UESP has no page for it, and the Velothi are canon for this coast.
Anvadas has no residents. The Oxhu and Agaceph keep clear of the mud-ridge. The household's ghosts stay in the flooded courtyard and the tower.
The ruin is half-swallowed by marsh. The Oxhu and Agaceph alike avoid it.
Ancestor ghosts in the lower halls, a humming sealed door and the river crocodiles.
Once a river-fort. The Agaceph trade ash-glass shards from its upper halls.

The household's ancestor tablets and altar niches survive in the upper halls, where Yina's readers copy them with respect. The lower hall's Daedric shrine is shut. The Agaceph say that it should stay shut.
The Cantemiric Velothi built it and the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 killed them; the Agaceph moved in at its foot soon after.
The sealed door hums at night. Yina's scholar will pay for anyone who can read the Velothi script above it.
A black stone keep with a broken tower on a river bank, ivy, vines, reed rafts moored under the wall.

Sethiral is a black stone keep with a broken tower and reed rafts moored under its wall. Yina's Agaceph read in the upper halls and the lower halls are shut. It is unnamed on the map; we named it in Velothi style. UESP has no page for it, and the Velothi are canon for this coast.
Sethiral's halls have no residents. Yina's Agaceph read in the upper rooms and leave at dusk. The household's ghosts keep to the lower halls, behind the humming door.
The upper halls are used by Yina's Agaceph as a reading place; the lower halls are shut.
Ghosts, collapsing floors and a sea-cave where the tide runs in.
Once a coastal watch-hold. Now a draw for scavengers and the occasional smuggler's cache.
The coastal hold kept the Velothi ancestor rites, with a niche and tablet for each family dead. The shrine in the lower hall served a Daedric power, and its spell-fire on the upper tier still burns.
Cantemiric Velothi built this coastal hold. The Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 ended them, and the headland has been unoccupied since.
A lamp-lit beacon on the upper tier still burns with a spell-fire; a captive Khiar fisherman was seen on it. A smuggler's cache lies in the sea-cave.
Black stone on a cliff edge, a broken sea-tower, salt crust, sea-birds nesting in the roof, surf below.

Mazurath crowns a sea-cliff above the surf, with a broken sea-tower that glows faintly after dark. It is unnamed on the map; we named it in Velothi style. UESP has no page for it, and the Velothi are canon for this coast.
Mazurath's headland has no residents. Khiar's villagers will not go up after dark. The household's ghosts are blamed for the glow on the sea-cliff.
A ruin on a sea-cliff, glowing faintly after dark, which the village of Khiar blames on its ghosts.
Cave-ins, poisonous gas in the lower galleries and a nest of crocodiles in the flooded drift.
Ochre for dye and alum for fixing it. Both go to Aroxhu's dyers; any surplus is sold to Archon.
The miners leave a pot of ochre at the mouth. Their dead are mourned in Aroxhu.
The Company's ochre and alum mine of the last Third Era, shut when the province closed in 4E 6; Aroxhu's clay-diggers and Seafalls families reopened the upper galleries.
The sealed galleries hold the Company's last strongbox. The gallery-boss wants a diver to see whether the flooded drift still connects.
A hillside cut in rust and yellow bands with a plank-lined adit, a Company-era timber headframe, ore carts, yellow-stained pools.
A mine on the road between Renhu and Seafalls whose Imperial-sounding name marks an East Empire Company working. UESP has no page for Vicrium.
About six miners, Oxhu clay-diggers and Seafalls families, led by a gallery-boss who keeps the key.
The upper galleries are worked in the dry season; the lower ones are sealed with clay plugs after a gas-pocket killed two men.
Ancestor ghosts, skeletal guards and a Sarpa lookout who will shoot anyone who approaches by air or reed-path.
Once a river-fort that taxed boat traffic. Now a scavenger's draw: Velothi bronze, ash-glass, ancestor tablets and a vault of stored dye-stuffs.
Mephala-influenced Velothi ancestor worship: altar niches to a Daedric lord and carved family tablets in every room.
Cantemiric Velothi held it until the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 ended them. The river gave it a boat road to the coast, which is our reading of its siting.
A house-lord's ghost still holds a ring of the family seal; the Dunmer relic-seller in Thorn will pay for the ring. The cistern is connected to the bight by a drowned tunnel.
Black stone courts and a tall broken tower in heavy Velothi courses, ivy and vines over the walls, a cistern with dark water in the heart.
A bigger Velothi ruin on a river bend behind the bight, with a Sarpa camp at its flank. It has no UESP page; the Velothi are canon for this seaboard.
No living folk inside. Velothi ancestor ghosts in the lower halls and a lich-like household warden are an AGENT_INVENTED guard.
Collapsed courts, a standing tower and a deep cistern, haunted. The Sarpa live beside it and take ash-glass and tablets from the edges but will not go into the lower halls.
Estuary tides, drunk sailors and smugglers; D1.
Rice, fish and reed sold on the water; a quiet trade in cargo that does not appear in customs books.
Sailors leave bits of net at a mud shrine for those drowned in the estuary.
Grew with Archon's trade: the tribe wanted a place to sell without entering the harbour and paying the dues.
A boat to hire into the bayou; a debt owed by an Archon pilot; goods that must pass customs unseen.
Stilt houses on the bank, a long plank landing, lanterns and boats; the town's lights are visible from the harbour.
A hamlet on the west bank of the estuary just above Archon, the transfer point between bayou rafts and harbour lighters.
Three Waters Argonians with Archon pilots as regular visitors; one old pilot's widow runs a lantern house.
Ten people hold the landing, sell to passing Archon boatmen and hear all that moves in the estuary.
Illusion traps and lost-looking reed paths; marsh crocodiles, leeches and fleshflies.
Reading fees, copied pages, illusion-work and eels. Prices are steep but fair.
They honour the Hist from a distance and read the missionary's tracts as comedy.
The hamlet grew round a mission library that its people took from a dead Maran outstation in the Third Era.
A page from the library has been cut out and sold; the librarian wants it back and will pay in books.
Raft-houses and stilts on a marsh pond, books drying on lines in the sun, rafts hauled onto reed beds.
A raft-and-stilt hamlet in the marsh between Gaweja and Renhu. No UESP page.
About seven Agaceph, with a literate eldest who acts as librarian and keeps a ledger.
A hamlet that guards its shelf of books and charges for access.
Safe by day. Smugglers land on the south bank at night; crocodiles in the paddies.
Rice, fish and ferry hire. The garrison buys at a fixed low price, which the farmers resent.
Sithis and a small village tree, with an Archein household still keeping a Divines-style roadside shrine.
Nothing is recorded. It is read as a farm settlement founded to feed the traders and garrison at the lake's south side after 4E 48.
The garrison's price dispute is close to a refusal by the farmers to sell; a stranger paid for a night's boat and left a sealed pouch behind; the south bank's smugglers want a dry store.
Stone-footed reed houses along a low shore, paddies fenced with reed, a small plank quay, and the fort's lamp visible across the water at dusk.
Yalugo is a hamlet of about six on the south lake shore between Truowa and the waters toward Korydon. It follows the Stormhold manner of raised stone footings; the name has no UESP page.
About six residents, Argonian farmers and a retired garrison cook of Archein descent.
Two farm families sell grain and smoked fish to Fort Gysilla and wayfarers, and keep a spare boat for anyone crossing to Luntoc or south toward Korydon.
Ancestor ghosts in the lower halls, illusions on the approach and river crocodiles.
Books, illusion-work and ash-glass shards; they trade a little with Renhu.
The Agaceph keep a respectful distance from the ruin's lower halls where the Velothi dead lie.
The Agaceph moved into the shell of a Velothi stronghold. They reuse its stone halls to store books and are not afraid of ghosts.
A sealed door in the ruin has begun to hum, and the scholar needs help opening it without waking the dead.
Raft-houses on the river, tied to the black Velothi wall, painted reed screens, books drying on the stone.
A hamlet at the river bank where a Cantemiric Velothi ruin stands, on the map's own pairing of a hamlet and a ruin in one cell. No UESP page for Yina.
About six Agaceph, with a scholar who has mapped the ruin's upper halls.
A hamlet of stilt-houses leaning against the ruin's wall. They defend it against Skeith raiders and tribal bands alike.
Fleshflies and crocodiles in the river mouth. The Tsonac men watch for the successors of Thorn's slavers and hold them in contempt.
Cut stone, hewn timber and lime go out to Thorn; salt, rope and cloth come in. Tsonac keeps the price of stone high. Thorn's buyers complain of it.
They carry small tokens of Tsonac's sleeping Hist and a tree-minder's charm of resin for sleeping. They do not pray to it in public.
Founded as a coast landing by Tsonac when Thorn's builders began buying stone again after the Great War. The freight path down from the jungle uplands is older than the hamlet.
A shipment of carved lintel stones for a Thorn client has gone missing between Tsonac and the jetty. The quarry-men suspect the smugglers on Skeith.
The landing has a neat dry-stone jetty with stacked blocks sorted by size, lime-white dust on the reeds and a few terraced stilt-houses with stone footings on the shore.
A hamlet at the bight's northern shore where the Tsonac-Kaleel's stone and timber reach the sea. It has no UESP page; its culture is Tsonac's by the map.
About six Argonians of Tsonac who move between the uplands and the shore, with a Thorn broker who lodges here during the dry months.
A busy river-mouth landing with a stone jetty, a lime kiln and loading sheds. Thorn boats call in the dry season.
Illusion and paralysis spells on strangers; otherwise the town is calm. The lake has crocodiles and a pirate-raft rumour.
Books, scrolls, ink, illusion-work and spell-teaching, sold for coin, fish and rice. Yulca's reading-room charges outsiders; its illusions are cheap.
No Hist grows here. The Agaceph find the Hist loud and prefer their books. They keep a hall of the Maran dead's tracts, which they read for sport.
The Agaceph gathered here after the Maran missions died in the Third Era. In canon they looted the Maran monastery at Umpholo for its library. Yulca keeps the most books of any place in the east.
The reading-room's most prized book has been stolen. A scholar wants a Maran tract translated. The readers of Yulca will not say why.
A town of lashed rafts and stilted pavilions on a broad lake, reed screens in bright scale-colours, a reading-room under a tall roof, books drying on lines, rafts like blades on the water.
A raft-town on a wide lake in the west, the only Agaceph place of any size. No UESP page for Yulca; the Agaceph are canon in Middle Argonia, exclusive to it.
About twenty-two Agaceph in rainbow colours; the council of readers has five members. A few visitors from Gaweja and Aroxhu live in a guest raft.
Yulca is a lake town of rafts with a public reading-room. Agaceph here are polite and wary and will freeze an intruder with a spell before deciding what to do.
Surf, crabs and hackwings on the shore; the station's folk do not like uninvited visitors and will report them to Helstrom.
Dried sea-salt, sea-kelp for dyeing, tide-wrack and eggs of sea-birds; they take in news and trade it for clay and pottery from Arorha.
Without a Hist near, they keep a sealed sap-jar from Helstrom on a shrine and read it as their counsel; they do not speak of the sea.
Founded when the Root-Folk wanted ears on the sea, after the Umbriel year; its people came from the Lake Ulaish country by canoe.
The sap-jar has gone cloudy and the elder fears the Hist is ill. A fresh jar must be carried from Helstrom, or the poison in this one must be found.
A cluster of reed-and-root stilt houses above the tide line, drying racks of kelp, canoes drawn up on mud, nets in a line.

A hamlet of Helstrom's people, set on the open coast far from any Hist tree. It has no UESP page; the Root-Folk's hunting and egg-tending stations spread through the inner swamp, and this is their sea outlier.
About five Saxhleel. The eldest has the status of a mid-ranked tree-minder and speaks to Helstrom through a sap-jar sent twice a year.
Five Root-Folk keep the station and rotate home after a season. They watch ships and trade quietly with Arorha.
